title: First three-string basses and who had four strings
summary: Foster recalls early New Orleans bassists having three-string basses, with Jimmy Brown the one with four.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: When I first started asking you about the number of strings on the bass, I wondered, way back when you were a kid, if you ever tried just the three strings. That's the first bass I had.

Three. Very few guys had full string basses. I remember around the North, all of them had three string basses. But a few guys you take like, well then, all of them guys, you know, Jimmy Brown had four strings. Jimmy, I think Jimmy Brown was the only one that had four string bass. Oh, Gaster too? Yeah, well, yeah. Oh, Gaster. Oh, Gaster.

Oaken had four strings. Yeah, yeah. Oaken, Oaken, Oaken, Oaken, Oaken. See, but Billy had three. Billy Marrera on him. Billy had three, three and four. Billy's the first string, you never put them on. Oh, Martin. I look. I look like, he looked to you with your first look at him. Like he's a selfish kind of a guy, but he's not.
